skills.name: safeguard-fallback-reroute
skills.description: Recover full-quality output when a safety classifier silently downgrades your session to a weaker fallback model, instead of accepting the fallback's degraded work as final.
skills.useFor: Noticing a silent model downgrade mid-session and working up a reframe/decompose/invert/escalate recovery ladder instead of retrying the same prompt or accepting the fallback's output as equivalent.

skills.name: pre-push-ship-checklist-template
skills.description: A six-gate checklist for shipping a change to any stateful service — ownership map, multi-source rule audit, structural gate, regression replay, safe restart, and one real end-to-end smoke test — run before every push.
skills.useFor: Shipping a change to a long-running stateful service where a broken deploy is expensive to notice after the fact, and building a ship checklist for a project that doesn't have one yet.

skills.name: cas-approval-gate
skills.description: An atomic compare-and-swap two-phase state machine that makes an autonomous agent's risky action provably impossible to execute without an explicit, allow-listed human's approval — closing the race-condition gap a plain "ask permission" flag leaves open.
skills.useFor: Pipelines where an autonomous agent proposes code-writing, spending, or state-mutating actions, and reviewing an existing approval flow for a race condition between checking and acting.

skills.name: verified-destination-routing-gate
skills.description: Before posting or mutating a single external destination, classify the payload into exactly one destination class and verify that destination against a freshly-read allowlist — never a cached ID — refusing on any ambiguity.
skills.useFor: Any bot or automation that posts to one of several possible external destinations, where sending to the wrong one would be embarrassing, unsafe, or hard to undo.

skills.name: cross-cli-delegation-preflight
skills.description: Operational hygiene rules for delegating work across multiple local AI CLIs or backends — a secretless read-only probe before any cross-tool call, a free-tier-first default, opaque aliases instead of real identifiers, and scoped, idempotent grants for any mutation triggered from a secondary surface.
skills.useFor: Any setup that routes tasks across more than one AI CLI or backend and needs consistent safety hygiene regardless of which one ends up doing the work.

skills.name: product-design-factory
skills.description: A design pipeline that grounds a product surface in one job statement, generates exactly three comparable design directions before picking one, compiles a token/component contract, builds one real vertical slice, and requires an independent hostile review before calling it done.
skills.useFor: Designing or redesigning a product surface where you want a genuine comparison between options and a real quality bar before shipping, not just the first workable idea.

skills.name: cross-vendor-verify-pipeline
skills.description: A three-role coding pipeline — one model plans, a second (different-vendor) model executes, and a third independently redoes the build/test run itself rather than reading the executor's diff — so "it passed" is never taken on the executor's word alone.
skills.useFor: Coding tasks important enough to want a genuine second opinion on execution quality, especially work you'll hand off and not watch step-by-step.

skills.name: hash-locked-plan-release
skills.description: Gate execution of any nontrivial plan behind a recorded consultation, an explicit user agreement, and a content-hash lock, so a plan can never run under an agreement that was given to a different version of it.
skills.useFor: Plan-then-execute agent workflows where a plan edit must always revoke a stale go-ahead, and pre-authorizing a proven low-risk revision class without loosening hard stops on destructive or scope-expanding changes.

skills.name: swarm-eligibility-gate
skills.description: Decide whether a task actually warrants fanning out multiple parallel agents before doing it, route eligible work across three generic roles with required-return contracts, and downgrade gracefully instead of silently duplicating work when a role is unavailable.
skills.useFor: Deciding whether a substantial task actually benefits from parallel agents before reaching for a fan-out by reflex, and choosing a safe downgrade when a swarm node times out or is unavailable.

skills.name: production-promotion
skills.description: Merge and verify an exact-SHA delivery candidate all the way into production — binding the merge commit, the deployed production SHA, and a live probe together — instead of treating a successful merge as a successful release.
skills.useFor: Promoting an already-verified PR into production and proving the live site is actually serving that exact commit, not just that the merge button worked.

skills.name: headless-agent-launch-verification
skills.description: Launch a headless/background CLI coding-agent run so it can't silently hang or lie about completing, and verify what it actually did instead of trusting its self-report.
skills.useFor: Delegating substantial work to a background CLI coding agent, and debugging a run that came back suspiciously empty.

skills.name: sandboxed-cli-worker-controller
skills.description: Run other AI coding CLIs as least-privilege, evidence-producing workers under one controller — stripped credentials and config, pinned binaries, content-free immutable receipts, and safe process-group cancellation.
skills.useFor: Getting an independent second CLI agent's review or fan-out work without handing it full local permissions, credentials, or config.

skills.name: code-graph-blast-radius
skills.description: Before editing a shared symbol, class, file, or module, query a code-dependency-graph tool for its actual upstream callers instead of relying on grep alone, then compare what you actually changed against the predicted blast radius afterward.
skills.useFor: Refactors, renames, or edits to shared utilities where you need to know what could break before you touch it.

skills.name: delegation-brief-contract
skills.description: A fixed structure for the handoff brief when an orchestrating loop delegates implementation work to an agent — the mechanism, an exclusive working path, hard prohibitions, exact gates, the proof standard, the stop line, and the report format.
skills.useFor: Writing a delegation brief that doesn't turn into rework, and verifying what a delegated agent reports back.

skills.name: backup-recoverability-canary
skills.description: Before treating an encrypted off-site backup as grounds to delete local originals, prove round-trip recoverability with a synthetic canary and independently escrow the recovery key — instead of trusting 'upload succeeded.'
skills.useFor: Deleting local originals after backing them up to an encrypted remote, and periodically re-checking an existing backup's recoverability.

skills.name: interface-quality-gate
skills.description: A mechanical-plus-visual quality gate for any UI — an AI-tells lint pass, multi-viewport screenshot checks for overlap/clipping/responsive states, and a frontend-standards checklist — run before calling an interface done.
skills.useFor: Reviewing any generated or edited web page, app screen, dashboard, or mobile layout for AI-slop and responsive-state defects.

skills.name: agent-prompt-architecture
skills.description: A repeatable method for designing and auditing an AI agent's system prompt, always-loaded rules file, tool-use guidance, and memory/compaction instructions — identify the surface, define one behavior target, remove obsolete scaffolding, verify with the smallest probe.
skills.useFor: Improving a system prompt or rules file that isn't producing the behavior you want, or auditing one for bloat and contradictions before adding to it.

skills.name: terminal-ui-quality-guardrail
skills.description: Review terminal and text-interface changes for clear hierarchy, readable contrast, keyboard-visible state, and useful status information before treating a visual change as complete.
skills.useFor: Reviewing a terminal theme, status line, prompt, pane layout, or text interface after a visual change.

skills.name: safe-cross-tool-configuration-transfer
skills.description: Transfer a useful workflow pattern between developer tools by inspecting configuration safely, translating intent into the target tool native surface, and verifying the smallest reversible change.
skills.useFor: Adapting a rule, command, hook, skill, or integration from one developer tool to another without copying private configuration.

skills.name: coherent-product-design-workflow
skills.description: Turn a product change into a coherent interface by defining the user job and states first, compiling reusable visual and interaction rules, then verifying the primary journey across real conditions.
skills.useFor: Designing or redesigning a product surface so its states, components, accessibility, and visual rules remain coherent.

skills.name: agent-history-recall
skills.description: Build a queryable local catalog of every past AI-agent session, decision, and note, then answer "what did we decide about X / why does Y work this way" via hybrid search over the catalog instead of re-reading raw transcript trees or guessing from model memory.
skills.useFor: Answering "what did we decide about X" from your own project history instead of guessing or re-reading old transcripts.

skills.name: ai-eval-rigor-checklist
skills.description: A checklist of ~20 evidence-grounded rules for evaluating AI models, agents, and RAG pipelines rigorously — eval design, retrieval-grounding tests, agent-trajectory grading, and precise language for deletion/unlearning claims.
skills.useFor: Reviewing an eval harness, benchmark, or RAG/agent grading setup before trusting its numbers.

skills.name: workspace-lease
skills.description: A file-leasing protocol that lets multiple concurrent AI-agent sessions — across separate git worktrees or clones of the same repository — claim exclusive write ownership of exact paths before editing, with atomic scoped commits and cross-worktree overlap detection.
skills.useFor: Running multiple AI-agent sessions against worktrees or clones of the same repo without them clobbering each other's edits.

skills.name: graph-engineering
skills.description: Design multi-agent work as a real directed graph instead of a chain — bounded nodes with explicit input/output contracts, edges only for genuine data dependencies, a fan-out/reduce/synthesize pattern, and isolated verifiers that never share context with the work they're checking.
skills.useFor: Designing or auditing a multi-agent fan-out pipeline for hidden fake edges and shared-context verifiers.

skills.name: cloud-delivery
skills.description: Treat "delivered" as an exact-commit-SHA state machine — bind a pushed branch to a verified CI pass and a matching preview deployment at that same SHA, and refuse to call anything shipped from a stale, mismatched, or inferred signal.
skills.useFor: Proving a pushed branch is actually good — CI and preview both verified at the exact same commit SHA — before calling it shipped.

skills.name: scoping-cutting
skills.description: An MVP-scoping framework combining Shape Up appetite-setting, "cut the list in half twice," an end-to-end "scooter not axle" value test, Wizard-of-Oz testing before automating, and an upfront kill-on-time commitment.
skills.useFor: Defining MVP scope or fighting scope creep on a feature that keeps growing.

skills.name: changelog-generator
skills.description: Generate consistent, auditable release notes directly from Conventional Commits — auto-detects the correct MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH semver bump, renders a Keep a Changelog-style document, and pairs with a CI commit-format linter and a mandatory human-approval gate.
skills.useFor: Auto-drafting release notes and the correct semver bump straight from Conventional Commits.

skills.name: api-design-reviewer
skills.description: A static REST API design review — lints naming/method/status-code/error-format conventions, diffs two spec versions to classify breaking vs. non-breaking changes, audits the versioning strategy, and produces a weighted design scorecard.
skills.useFor: Reviewing a REST API's design consistency before it ships, or diffing two spec versions for breaking changes.

skills.name: architecture-decision-records
skills.description: Capture architectural decisions as structured ADRs (Michael Nygard format) the moment they're made — auto-detects decision moments, extracts context/alternatives/consequences, and only ever writes a file after explicit user approval.
skills.useFor: Capturing why a significant architecture choice was made, in a structured, approved, indexed ADR.

skills.name: runbook-generator
skills.description: Generate a standardized operational runbook for a service — start/stop/health-check/maintenance/incident-response/rollback/escalation sections, each critical step paired with an expected-output verification check.
skills.useFor: Writing an operational runbook for a service whose every critical step is paired with a verification check.

skills.name: observable-share
skills.description: Before anything gets shared outward, require three written answers (what's the one thing this says, what live source backs every number, what watches it and fixes it when it breaks), plus a hard word budget and a 'stale must look stale' rule.
skills.useFor: Any report, dashboard, or status post with numbers in it, especially catching staleness that looks healthy.

skills.name: overnight-product-factory
skills.description: An unattended build-and-deploy pipeline that only ships on a hard gate — a unique canary token must round-trip through both the QA probe and the live health probe, and a failed deploy triggers an independently-verified rollback.
skills.useFor: Handing a defined product idea to an agent overnight and getting back a trustworthy SHIPPED/BUILT/STOPPED_AT_GATE report instead of an unverified 'done' claim.

skills.name: second-machine-offload
skills.description: Turn a second machine you own into a safe batch worker for CPU-bound jobs — a health check, a secrets-excluding file sync, and a single round-trip command with a verifiable receipt.
skills.useFor: Offloading compiles, transcodes, test sweeps, or bulk data jobs off your primary machine without ever putting its credentials on the second one.

skills.name: ci-triage
skills.description: Triage every red CI run across your repos by classifying each failure's root signature — infrastructure 'never started' vs. a genuine 'step failed' — so a rerun is only attempted on the classes it can actually fix.
skills.useFor: Stopping a billing outage or runner regression from being misdiagnosed as a wave of unrelated flaky tests.

skills.name: deletion-safety-gate
skills.description: Before deleting a worktree, clone, or cache, run a fail-closed reference check across scheduled jobs, config files, running processes, and shared git object stores — SAFE only if every screen completes and finds zero references.
skills.useFor: Any bulk cleanup or 'reclaim disk space' pass, so you never delete a directory a scheduled job is still executing out of.

skills.name: gate-erosion-audit
skills.description: Audit an existing safety gate or verifier for five specific ways enforcement silently stops working — fail-open on error, opt-in-by-default, self-supplied evidence, a single unenforced entry point, and asymmetric normalization.
skills.useFor: Reviewing a gate you're about to trust more, or after a 'the gate should have caught this' incident.

skills.name: skill-suite-router
skills.description: Once a personal AI-agent skill library grows past a few dozen entries, group related skills behind thin 'suite' router skills that only route, so the top-level skill list stays short and trigger phrases stop colliding.
skills.useFor: A skill/command library that's gotten long enough that two skills compete for the same trigger phrasing.

skills.name: compaction-contract
skills.description: A fixed five-section template for summarizing long AI-agent sessions that quotes exact strings (paths, errors, flags) instead of paraphrasing them.
skills.useFor: Long agentic sessions that get compacted or handed off, so the next session resumes without re-deriving state.

skills.name: adversarial-planning
skills.description: A deep-planning protocol: parallel research agents map current state and blast radius, competing designs are drafted, then a mandatory adversarial pass attacks the plan before any implementation.
skills.useFor: Non-trivial features, refactors, migrations, and anything handed to an autonomous agent to execute unattended.

skills.name: model-lane-routing
skills.description: Stable role-to-model-tier lanes — the strongest model plans and verifies, a cheaper capable model executes, a different-vendor long-context model judges — with live-pricing re-verification before cost-based decisions.

skills.name: fanout-cost-pinning
skills.description: Explicitly pin every spawned subagent to the cheapest adequate model tier, closing the silent-inheritance leak where parallel readers run on the apex-priced main-loop model.

skills.name: multi-cli-constitution
skills.description: Keep multiple AI coding CLIs behaviorally consistent with one shared constitution file, a capability routing table with polyfill recipes, and a compiled policy block injected identically into each tool's config.
skills.useFor: The day you add a second AI coding CLI, or after two tools behave differently on the same rule.

skills.name: background-agent-roster
skills.description: The twelve standing background agents worth running on any machine hosting unattended AI automation, plus the receipt-file and whitelisted-autofix discipline that keeps the roster honest.
skills.useFor: Growing a scheduled-automation estate without silent multi-week outages.

skills.name: agent-memory-sync
skills.description: A git-backed persistent memory layout for AI agents — one fact per file with typed frontmatter, an always-loaded index, and a scheduled commit/rebase/push sync job.
skills.useFor: Making what an agent learned survive session boundaries, machine switches, and agent-tool switches.

skills.name: chat-platform-agent-bridge
skills.description: Wire an external chat platform (Telegram, Discord, SMS, etc.) into an AI agent so you can send it a prompt from your phone and get the reply back in the same chat, with untrusted-input quarantining and sender allow-listing built in.
skills.useFor: Sending your agent a prompt from your phone while away from your desk, or building a lightweight remote control for an unattended agent without exposing a web endpoint.

skills.name: production-quality-autopatch-loop
skills.description: Continuously score live production conversation/interaction transcripts against a quality rubric, auto-draft a minimal prompt-only fix as a pull request, and auto-merge it only once it clears a strict multi-reviewer safety gate.
skills.useFor: A deployed conversational or text-generating product where you want quality regressions caught from real traffic and small prompt fixes shipped automatically, never auto-merging an unreviewed or oversized change.

skills.name: agent-burst-resource-prep
skills.description: A pre-flight routine that frees RAM and drops memory pressure on your machine so it can safely run a larger batch of parallel AI-agent sessions than usual, then restores normal state afterward.
skills.useFor: Right before spawning a larger-than-normal parallel AI-agent fan-out, or after noticing a big parallel run swapping/thrashing instead of speeding up.

skills.name: architecture-invariant-audit
skills.description: A read-only, dependency-free script that checks a layered codebase against documented architecture rules (layer crossings, legacy reuse, anti-pattern regressions, doc drift) and fails CI when they're violated.
skills.useFor: Enforcing a layered architecture boundary, tracking a strangler-pattern legacy file's shrink, or catching a previously-fixed anti-pattern before it regresses elsewhere.

skills.name: policy-prompt-drift-check
skills.description: Compares a code-level policy module against the natural-language prompt it governs, flags missing anchors and direct ALLOW/FORBID contradictions, and emits a per-policy ALIGNED/WARN/DRIFT verdict without editing anything.
skills.useFor: Before merging a PR that touches a policy/constants module shared with a prompt file, or after any prompt rewrite.

skills.name: git-identity-guard
skills.description: Pre-push check that verifies the active git author email, authenticated gh CLI account, and target remote all match what you declared for this repo, and refuses to push on any mismatch or missing declaration.
skills.useFor: Working across a personal and a work GitHub account (or several client accounts) on the same machine.

skills.name: safe-project-retirement
skills.description: Enumerate every surface tied to a dead project (repos, scheduled jobs, dashboards, notes), get human confirmation, then archive everything reversibly with an undo manifest instead of deleting it.
skills.useFor: Cleaning up a finished or abandoned project without hunting down every cron job and dashboard entry by hand.

skills.name: cross-repo-work-recap
skills.description: Pull a structured, evidence-backed recap (shipped / in-flight / at-risk) of work across multiple local git repos over a time window, cross-referenced with personal notes.
skills.useFor: Answering 'what did you actually get done this week' across several repos without reconstructing it from memory.

skills.name: agent-observability-bundle
skills.description: Build a fully-local, zero-cost observability bundle for an AI coding agent — a status line, a hallucination-blocking turn-end hook, and an optional periodic quality grader.
skills.useFor: Getting visibility into context usage, cost, and unverified 'done' claims from your AI coding agent without a paid monitoring service.

skills.name: text-to-image-bakeoff
skills.description: Wraps OpenAI gpt-image-1, Fal's Flux Pro, and Google Imagen text-to-image APIs behind one small script with a bake-off comparison mode, backend health tracking, and a reusable prompt template.
skills.useFor: Generating hero art or concept backdrops when no image-generation MCP/tool is available, or comparing providers before picking a default.

skills.name: evidence-gated-delegation
skills.description: Before letting a secondary agent, worker fleet, or automation pipeline act on your behalf, require a proven track record plus deterministic post-hoc verification — never trust the delegate's own self-report of success.
skills.useFor: Wiring up a second agent or automation pipeline that will act without your eyes on every step.

skills.name: legitimate-work-reroute
skills.description: Recover full-quality output when a safety classifier misreads legitimate, authorized defensive-security work as an attack because of how the request is worded, without ever using this to evade a genuine restriction.
skills.useFor: An authorized defensive-security task comes back visibly weaker or refused because it was worded in attack-shaped language.

skills.name: environment-drift-hunter
skills.description: Runs a scheduled and on-demand battery of deterministic, no-LLM checks over a local dev/automation setup and surfaces a ranked, evidence-backed finding list with concrete fixes and an autofix-safe flag.
skills.useFor: Catching doc-vs-code drift, orphan jobs, security-default drift, and committed secrets before they turn into a real incident.

skills.name: negative-prompt-leakage
skills.description: When writing FORBIDDEN/NEVER/✗ example blocks in an LLM prompt, never spell out the literal forbidden phrase — models pattern-match into the bad example and reproduce it; use a short abstract marker instead.
skills.useFor: Prompts where the model keeps producing an output you explicitly told it never to produce.

skills.name: fail-closed-guards
skills.description: When a guard/gate/precondition depends on data that might be missing, make the missing-data fallback REFUSE the action, not allow it — and confirm every write-site actually populates the field the guard reads.
skills.useFor: Writing or reviewing any permission check, gate, or precondition with a fallback default.

skills.name: twilio-a2p-10dlc-compliance
skills.description: Get a Twilio 10DLC A2P SMS campaign approved, or un-stick a rejected one — decodes the common rejection codes and covers the non-obvious resubmission mechanics.
skills.useFor: A FAILED/rejected Twilio A2P campaign, or building an SMS opt-in flow before submitting one.

skills.name: skill-estate-guardian
skills.description: Continuously lint your own AI-agent tooling (skills, subagent definitions, workflow scripts, hooks) for the defect classes that quietly rot an agent estate — leaked tokens, retired model IDs, unpinned models, gate docs with no real enforcement.
skills.useFor: A pre-flight check after writing/editing a skill or agent, or a periodic cleanup pass over your whole skills directory.

skills.name: roast-me
skills.description: Multi-round adversarial questioning that forces you to defend a design BEFORE you build it — generates hard questions across failure modes, edge cases, security, and performance, then iterates on your answers.
skills.useFor: Stress-testing a plan or architecture decision before you commit to building it.

skills.name: ai-tells-check
skills.description: A pre-flight linter for the highest-signal 'AI-slop' tells in generated frontend/marketing copy — em-dashes, numbered eyebrows, BETA labels, generic filler phrases, decorative status dots.
skills.useFor: A fast last check after generating any landing page, hero section, or marketing UI.

skills.name: data-illustration
skills.description: Turn a set of scores/metrics into an accurate AND illustrative graphic — the data literally drives the shape of the artwork, so it reads as a designed illustration instead of a generic chart.
skills.useFor: Visualizing scores/metrics/dimensions when a plain bar/line/pie chart would be boring or off-brand.

skills.name: agent-engineering-checklist
skills.description: A curated checklist of ~18 evidence-grounded rules for building reliable AI agents — tool-use gating, verification-before-trust, context engineering, and safety/trust boundaries.
skills.useFor: Designing a new agent/workflow, or reviewing an existing one for reliability gaps before more autonomous use.

skills.name: agent-quality-loop
skills.description: Iteratively grade and improve a conversational AI agent's prompt quality without real end-users — synthetic dialogs, hard checks + an LLM judge, targeted human-approved prompt edits until quality plateaus.
skills.useFor: After any meaningful change to a conversational agent's system prompt, or as a regression gate before a demo/release.

skills.name: ai-ugc-video-pipeline
skills.description: A hardened, gated pipeline for producing short-form AI-generated 'UGC-style' marketing video — hard-won fixes for the media-validation, audio-sync, and judge-hallucination traps that silently ship broken output.
skills.useFor: Producing or re-cutting a short-form AI-presenter product/marketing video.

skills.name: expert-fanout
skills.description: Spawn N domain-expert subagents in parallel to audit a codebase, product, or design from different angles, then synthesize convergent vs. divergent recommendations.
skills.useFor: Breaking out of a surgical-patch loop, getting a second opinion before a risky change, comparing two architecture options.

skills.name: doc-iterate
skills.description: Process inline review-comment markers left in shared Markdown docs, apply edits in place, preserve history, and flag contradictions instead of guessing.
skills.useFor: Async doc review between collaborators without a full comment/suggestion system.

skills.name: bug-replay
skills.description: Turn every fixed bug into a permanent regression fixture and replay the whole set before you ship anything.
skills.useFor: Catching regressions on bugs you already fixed, building a growing regression suite from real incidents.

skills.name: ship-as-artifact
skills.description: Render any finished deliverable (report, brief, plan, design, mockup) as a self-contained hosted page and hand over the link instead of a terminal dump.
skills.useFor: Reports, briefs, audits, roadmaps, and design/mockup previews meant to be read, reviewed, or shared.

skills.name: offload
skills.description: Route self-contained work off your primary AI assistant's metered quota onto a secondary backend you already have, then verify the result yourself.
skills.useFor: Being low on quota, parallelizing independent work, or getting an independent second opinion.

skills.name: quality-gate-registry
skills.description: Map every 'done' claim to the specific proof required before you say it out loud.
skills.useFor: Preventing confidently reporting unverified tests, builds, deploys, or fixes as complete.

skills.name: staff-code-review
skills.description: A maximum-depth, multi-agent code review that auto-locates the diff, fans out a cross-functional panel, adversarially verifies findings, and synthesizes a prioritized risk register.
skills.useFor: Pre-merge high-stakes diffs and production-readiness audits.

skills.name: production-gauntlet
skills.description: A looped, dual-verification stress-test and KPI gate to run before calling any non-trivial change 'done'.
skills.useFor: Wanting genuine walk-away quality on anything non-trivial you've built, fixed, or deployed.

skills.name: autobuild-loop
skills.description: An end-to-end, self-verifying build pipeline (plan, swarm, docs, QA, code quality, canary, summary) gated stage-by-stage on verification artifacts.
skills.useFor: A defined-end-state build you want to walk away from and trust came back correct.

skills.name: skill-miner
skills.description: Mine your own AI-assistant session transcripts for repeated workflow patterns and draft candidate reusable skills, queued for human approval.
skills.useFor: Discovering which of your repeated multi-step workflows would make good reusable skills.
